title: Honest question: why so much hate for games made with AI help?
author: SvenPatrick
selftext:
I got into game dev a few years ago but never shipped anything. Between my job and my family there was never much time, and the biggest wall was always assets. Whatever I could make myself never came close to what I had in my head, and that killed most projects early.

AI changed that. I now build games for jams and just for fun, and I actually finish them. For the first time in years, game dev feels like a hobby again instead of a folder full of abandoned prototypes.

What I don’t get is the amount of hate. If a game is great, I don’t care whether GenAI was involved. If it’s bad, it’s bad, with or without AI. For me, the result is what counts.

So, honest question: are we all just dumb over here? Am I missing the point? Is it mostly artists worried about their jobs? Or people who see every new technology as evil, the kind who’d still ride horses because cars are the devil?

Genuinely curious, especially if you were skeptical yourself at some point.

comments.author: mile-high-guy
comments.body: Bla bla bla spam

comments.author: spiress
comments.body: because 99% of ai made games are low effort garbage, “devs” even don’t fully test it lol

replies.author: SvenPatrick
replies.body: That may be true or it may not be true. But even great games that use AI generated assets get so much hate. I know some good examples. And yes, that's my point. Critzise a game because it sucks, not because it was created with or without the help of GenAI.

replies.author: Baraga91
replies.body:
The majority of absolutely garbage games that get published recently are what u/spireas and u/RhinostrilBe describe, which creates a kneejerk response from people not actively working on game dev (read: most gamers) because they all share a common thread. They use AI. 

We can rise above that critique and distance ourselves from the trash, but we can't ignore the facts.

comments.author: RhinostrilBe
comments.body: Many people have an irresponsibly low bar of quality they push out to the world. They flood the same channels to grab attention for a game that is not polished. And people in turn get resentful

replies.author: SvenPatrick

replies.author: Silver-Chipmunk7744

replies.author: SvenPatrick
replies.body: That’s true for so many areas of life with all the technological progress over the last few decades. And since I’m not the youngest anymore, I’ve seen a few of those cycles myself. But I get your point. Once this becomes normal, things will shift, just like they did in every big cycle before.

replies.author: RhinostrilBe
replies.body: Unity devs got critiqued for pushing shovelware out the door a while ago. I reckon with genAI it has gotten at least 10x easier to make a game. The result is lots of beginners making lots of beginner mistakes out in public

comments.author: PositiveScarcity8909
comments.body: Sloppy games

comments.author: Particular-Win-1291
comments.body: Because the games are trash

comments.author: FragmentedHeap
comments.body:
Because most of them are one shot frim a Claude prompt with devs pushing them desperate to make money and flooding the market with garbage. 

If you used artificial intelligence to build your own tools and spent a whole year painstakingly making a video game and going over every out of it and checking its quality and its performance and it's really really good. 

Then that's amazing and that's what we want to see. 

But if you spend a weekend with Claude and threw a thing up on the web and it's just utter garbage nobody cares

Artificial intelligence is extremely powerful and I want to see people  do something great with it. 

I expect the quality of coming out of an AI produced video game to be higher than any human or team of humans could have done the bar that I want to see hit is hundreds of times higher than most people are hitting. 

I want to play a game that was so good that everybody playing it will realize that it wouldn't have been possible to make it without artificial intelligence. 

I want to see the technology pull out innovation and inspiration and effort that is many times higher than most AAA game companies are producing. 

Nobody wants to play some slop somebody made in a couple of days. 

They want to play something that's going to leave their jaw on the ground for 3 weeks after they finish playing it where they will never feel satisfied playing other games because they just had their mind blown.

We should be seeing AI games where their creators made more creative games. 

Not less creative games

replies.author: SvenPatrick
replies.body:
Absolutely. A shitty game is a shitty game. And yes, I also think it’s a real problem that the few gems get buried under the flood of low-effort stuff. But like with every new technology, once the big wave passes, the amount of low-quality games will shrink.

It’s like the early days of the internet. Only a handful of people could build a website. Then website builders came along and the internet got flooded with crappy sites. But the market sorted it out, like it always does. And did anyone ever say “your website sucks because you didn’t code it from scratch”?

comments.author: mike_hoff
comments.body: I think different people have different issues. One example might be that it’s trained on work of others without them being compensated. comments.author: InSilicoAwards
comments.body: I think it helps if you think about the actual labor costs in a project and advertise that. I had Claude do a calculation of a game remake I'm building, and just off programming + art assets it would be anywhere between $700k-2.5 million to develop it. But I've been working at it for weeks now, not push button.

comments.author: Richard_Philip
comments.body:
Most logical reason I heard was that it takes away work from artists...   
In my case? I started using it and despite the repetitions to get something good out of it, it is way faster than drawing everything by myself.  
And of the flip side... I could not afford an artist to do the job. so no work was taken away from anyone. :D   
I was sceptical at first because especially years ago the images they created was unusable (spaceships with pig ears and such... )   
But lately they become good. still need a lots of refinement, but it can generate almost anything. With a good prompt and clear vision on the human side...

replies.author: SvenPatrick
replies.body: For me, it actually sparks creativity, because my huge lack of artistic skill isn’t holding me back anymore :D

comments.author: sevenoutdb
comments.body: It’s changing - but most importantly- we need to make great games

comments.author: HaMMeReD
comments.body:
The equation is changing, people just aren't use to it.

The transition is not kind either. I mean 1-4yr skill building and implementation got compressed to 5 minutes for a naive person.

If you spent 4 years learning to program, do art, sound etc. Stayed up all night, traded your life for something, and then someone can grab that and clone it in 5 minutes, the moat has been sucked up around you. I want to acknowledge that I get it, I understand.

But at the same time, it's sunken cost fallacy and crab bucket mentality. They invested time, and that has to have meant something, so they need to double down to not see it as time wasted, and they attack others as "thieves" or any other argument they can make up, and move goal posts around like "code is ok, images are not".

That said, I don't think it's time wasted at all, technical skills provide a layer of knowledge that lets you go farther than a basic vibe coder. I don't think that part of the meta will change. Understanding how a game works is a challenge on many different dimensions of knowledge.

It's also about personal taste, i.e. using generative images in a game right now is a risky move, and you'll alienate a huge part of your demographic. But if you use code for 100%, somehow it's OK as long as the community deems it "ai assisted" and not "vibe coding" for the most part. The anti-generative image/model/sound crowd is more rabid than the coding at this time. But coding was here first, it was just like this a year ago for code. People will get over other aspects as well at least some of them.

comments.author: Jacmac_
comments.body: Most people don't care if AI was used, but a lot of people are afraid of what AI can do. When you really get down to the nuts and bolts arguments it's all a fear of what it means for jobs. I don't blame these people for being fearful, but you can't let this fear become irrational.

comments.author: SeaBuilding3911
comments.body:
Because they sell assets.

Reddit indie game ecosphere is an asset market. They are here to sell their assets all day long. 

We are seeing a dying industry.

comments.author: CoolTIOnline
comments.body:
As someone who's new at game dev and use AI, I think the hate comes for many different reasons such as:  
\-Flood of lazy games made in literal days.  
\-Killing of Art  
\-Impact on software dev jobs  
...  
It really depends who you ask. I understand the frustration towards it but in the end, it's a tool and as much as there is some bad coming from it, there is a lot of good.  
It enables a lot of people who actually put serious effort into their projects to create great things.

I could argue for the slop games that those existed even before AI was a thing. It's just that with AI they can be made in a single day.

comments.author: santigv1500
comments.body: I think it depends on the genre as well, for example on cozy World,  most players not only like the game but the history behind it, the effort put on it, and the talento, AI does not require to much talent on so many stuffs, personally i dont care to much about it , but i alao dislike the big amount of AI Slop flooding the game stores, and i know before AI we had shitty games too, but this particual too allow to growth the list exponentially

comments.author: monchikun
comments.body:
We're looking at the wrong problem and getting distracted by "feelings" and "sentiment". We're barrelling towards a supply/demand problem. Sentiment for AI assisted game dev will continue to change and when it becomes widely accepted as part of producing and shipping titles what do you think happens to the supply/demand problem?

The noise is distracting you from the cliff that many of us are heading towards.

comments.author: fisj
comments.body: Since last week we're removing posts that essentially boil down to talking about AI sentiment outside this sub. We get multiple of these posts a day, and we want to refocus discussion around actual development using AI.
